t: LeetCode 1619 — Mean of Array After Removing Some Elements
o: Trim the smallest 5% and the largest 5% of arr, then average what remains. Because arr.length is guaranteed to be a multiple of 20, both trims remove an exact integer count k = n/20 elements — no rounding ambiguity. Example 1 has n = 20, k = 1: dropping the lone 1 and lone 3 leaves eighteen 2's, so the mean is exactly 2. In Example 2, removing one 0 and one 10 leaves sum 72 over 18 elements, giving 4. Since only order statistics matter, sorting immediately exposes the kept middle block; the 10^-5 acceptance tolerance means plain floating-point summation suffices.
k: n being a multiple of 20 makes the 5% trims exact integers: drop exactly k = n/20 elements off each end.
After sorting, the answer is just the mean of the middle block arr[k .. n-k-1] — no simulation needed.
Values are capped at 10^5, so a counting array achieves O(n + V) without comparison sorting.

a.n: Approach 1: Sort and Average the Middle
a.i: Sort ascending, skip the first k and last k entries, sum the rest with a wide accumulator and divide by n - 2k. The most direct faithful implementation of the statement.
s: Sum arr[k] through arr[n-k-1] using a 64-bit accumulator.
a.t: O(n log n) — the sort dominates; the summation sweep is linear.
a.sp: O(1) auxiliary beyond the sort's internal usage.

a.i: Since every value lies in [0, 10^5], tally occurrences per value. Sweep values upward consuming a removal budget of k to drop the smallest elements, then sweep downward consuming another budget of k to drop the largest — each kept occurrence contributes its value to the running total. This is a counting sort fused with the trimming step, achieving linear time in the value range.
s: Ascending pass: consume the low-trim budget of k, adding kept counts times value to the total.
Descending pass: consume the high-trim budget of k, subtracting removed counts times value.
a.t: O(n + V) — one pass over arr plus one over the value range V = 100001.

w:
## Wrap-up

The sorting version is the interview default — say "k = n/20" out loud to show you exploited the divisibility guarantee. **Pitfalls:** integer division truncating the mean (cast before dividing); wrong slice bounds (Python's arr[k:n-k] naturally excludes index n-k, but off-by-one errors are easy elsewhere); 32-bit overflow of the running sum in untyped or C-style languages.

**Edge cases:** all-equal arrays; duplicates straddling both trims simultaneously (the counting version handles a value consumed by both budgets). **Follow-ups:** a streaming variant where values cannot all be stored — use two heaps for online quantile trimming, or approximate with P2/T-Digest sketches.
